text:
rina: Hi all, on my first day trying to run the dev stack. I ran `docker compose up` and the postgres service keeps exiting. Logs show `FATAL: could not bind IPv4 socket: Address already in use` then later `could not open socket "/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432": No such file or directory`. I'm on macOS Ventura with an existing Postgres installed via Postgres.app. Not sure which to kill or change. Anyone?

josh: welcome! if you have a host postgres running on 5432 and your compose maps `5432:5432` that'll cause the address-in-use error. Postgres inside the container may also try sockets. Can you paste your compose postgres section?

rina: here's what the repo has (from docker-compose.yml):
```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:14
    ports:
      - 5432:5432
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: devpass
```

emily: seems normal. Two common flows: 1) stop your host postgres (Postgres.app or `brew services stop postgresql`) to free port 5432 and then bring up compose; OR 2) change the host port mapping to avoid collision, e.g. `- 5433:5432` and update app DB host/port env.

josh: also, the socket error might happen if your client is trying to connect over a Unix socket on the host instead of TCP to the container. Check for `DATABASE_URL` or `PGHOST` in your shell. If you have `PGHOST=/var/run/postgresql` your client will try socket. For compose dev use `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:devpass@postgres:5432/redwood` or set `DB_HOST=postgres` in `.env.local`.

rina: stopped Postgres.app and restarted `docker compose up`  postgres starts but the web app still errors with `could not connect to server: No such file or directory` referencing `/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432`. I thought stopping the host would have fixed it.

emily: did you restart your terminal or shell? Sometimes `PGHOST` is exported in your shell session and persists. Run `env | grep -i pg` and `echo $DATABASE_URL`. Also double-check `docker compose ps` to ensure the postgres container is named `postgres` and healthy.

rina: aha `echo $DATABASE_URL` returns `postgres:///redwood` from a previous project. That explains the socket attempt. Unsetting it and adding `DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:devpass@postgres:5432/redwood` in `.env.local` fixed the web app connecting. :tada:

josh: nice. For persisting data on mac, we recommend using a named volume to avoid filesystem permission issues with host binds: in compose add `volumes:\n  pgdata:` and use `- pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data`. If you need to access the DB from host tools, map host port to a non-conflicting port (5433) and run `psql -h localhost -p 5433 ...`.

emily: small onboarding tip: our `./dev` wrapper normally sets `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=redwood-dev` and supplies `DB_HOST=postgres` via `docker-compose.override.yml`. If you run `docker compose` manually, you might miss those overrides.

infra-bot: FYI: onboarding checklist item exists for "Local Postgres conflicts". Please open an issue if the wording could be clearer.

rina: thanks everyone. I'll open an issue with steps I took (stopped Postgres.app, unset old DATABASE_URL, switched to named volume) and link this thread so future new hires can find it. Filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/issues/105. Really appreciate the help! ❤️
